documents.description:
ARCHITECTURAL, LIVE, and it has already fired at least three times. A published paper's `body_html` is a BYTE-EXACT cache regenerated ONLY at publish time. At READ time, reader_source/3 -> conflicting_html_cache?/4 (content/papers.ex:133-138) re-renders the blocks with the CURRENT renderer and compares `rendered != html`; any difference is treated as a provenance error -> {:error, :ambiguous_source} -> HTTP 422. CONSEQUENCE: ANY change to the PortableDoc renderer silently 422s EVERY already-published paper that uses a touched block type. The paper is not edited, its blocks are valid, and it simply stops rendering. There is NO gate at merge time — the breakage surfaces days later in the scheduled paper-readers workflow, which was RED and UNREAD on main for three consecutive days (07-18, 07-19, 07-20). EVIDENCE: 4 papers were 422 on 2026-07-20. parity-state last published 2026-07-11; portabledoc-showcase 2026-07-18T04:16Z — both PREDATE the S-tier pdrender rounds that landed later on 07-18 (#4126, #4140, #4192) and the status-manifest change on 07-19 (#4394). gui-tui-parity-page carries a `status-legend` block, which #4394 touched. All three were repaired by nothing more than clearing body_html and republishing — i.e. by re-rendering with the CURRENT renderer, which only fixes anything if the stored cache had drifted. (The 4th, pds-crown-transcript-cold-beam-2026-07-20, was a DIFFERENT cause: legacy Portable Text blocks with no string `type`, rejected by valid_reader_blocks?/1. Do not conflate the two.) NOTE ON METHOD: an attempt to prove this by mutating a stored body_html measured NOTHING — publish regenerates the cache, so the mutation was overwritten and the page stayed 200. Any fix must be proven by a test that can actually fail; a republish-based mutation cannot. FIX DIRECTIONS: (a) prefer the canonical source — if blocks are valid, RENDER FROM BLOCKS and refresh the cache instead of 422ing; the 422 exists to avoid serving stale RICHER html, but blocks are canonical so preferring them is strictly safe; (b) version the cache — store the renderer version/digest next to body_html and regenerate on mismatch rather than erroring (this is the general rule that a cache must record what it DEPENDS on, not just what it is derived from); (c) a merge gate: any diff under portable_doc/render/ requires a re-render sweep over published papers; (d) make the scheduled audit's red actually reach someone. FIX BAR: a renderer change must not be able to 422 an unedited published paper, proven by MUTATION — change a renderer's output, show papers using that block still render.

PRECISION AUDIT BY THE LEAD (2026-07-20 ~14:40Z) — this task's own headline was OVERSTATED and is corrected here rather than left to mislead a builder. The causal chain has THREE links and they are NOT equally proven:
  LINK 1 — the byte-exact comparison exists. CONFIRMED AT L2 (read from origin/main, not the checkout): `git show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark/content/papers.ex` -> conflicting_html_cache?/4 ends in `rendered != html`, where `rendered` is a LIVE re-render via Render.render_blocks/2 and `html` is the stored cache. Any byte difference is a conflict.
  LINK 2 — a drifted cache produces HTTP 422. CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY: three papers (parity-state, portabledoc-showcase, gui-tui-parity-page) served 422 and every one returned to 200 after nothing but clearing body_html and republishing, which only helps if the stored cache had drifted.
  LINK 3 — a RENDERER CHANGE is what causes the drift. **INFERRED, NOT PROVEN.** The evidence is date alignment only: parity-state last published 07-11 and portabledoc-showcase 07-18T04:16Z, both predating the S-tier pdrender rounds later on 07-18 (#4126/#4140/#4192), and gui-tui-parity-page carries a status-legend block that #4394 touched. That is circumstantial. No renderer change has been observed to 422 a paper in a controlled test.
  SO THE HEADLINE 'ANY renderer change silently 422s EVERY published paper using a touched block type' is a HYPOTHESIS about link 3, resting on two confirmed links. Do not quote it as measured fact.
  A FALSIFICATION TEST WAS ATTEMPTED AND HAD NO POWER: zero commits touched portable_doc/render/ on origin/main after the repair, so 'papers still render 200' is exactly what BOTH the hypothesis and its negation predict. Recorded as inconclusive rather than as support.
  THE DECISIVE TEST, for whoever takes this: change a renderer's OUTPUT BYTES for one block type, do NOT republish any paper, and check whether an already-published paper using that block type flips 200 -> 422. That single experiment settles link 3 in either direction, and it is also criterion 2's mutation proof.

purpose.statement: Stop renderer changes from turning valid published papers into HTTP 422 while retaining divergence protection.
purpose.why: The larger publishing goal is that authors' papers remain readable as renderers evolve without silently preferring stale or divergent HTML. A global renderer-version bump made faithful older caches look indistinguishable from conflicting authored content, so hundreds of valid papers could fail together. Separating provenance classes and fixing every producer and recovery path was the right intervention because simply accepting mismatches would reintroduce content loss. If omitted, the next renderer edit can again take the published corpus offline or tempt operators into unsafe hand repair.
